findings.location: Decoded input, RAW row value (687,1002)-(700,1016), directly under SELECTOR value `0x1a2b3c4d` (687,975)
findings.finding: New this round. RAW now renders a bare em dash at the 14px value rung, in the row immediately beneath a row that renders four bytes of the very payload the dash denies — a selector IS the first bytes of the call data, so the pair reads as a contradiction rather than as one emptiness test. It also gives the page a third vocabulary for absence in three sections: a worded chip (AGE `No timestamp published`), worded sentences (Events, Internal calls, State changes), and now a glyph with no words at all, whose explanation is 45px below it in a separate card. Either label the row `ARGUMENTS`, or set RAW to the selector bytes it is a prefix of.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column: TYPE `public` (687,965) versus CANONICAL `Yes` (687,1046) and FINALITY `Pending` (687,1084)
findings.finding: Carried and re-verified by measurement. The value column runs at two type rungs for one class of data: `public` is plain 14px mono (x-height 7px, ascender 10px), while `Yes` and `Pending` are 12px letterspaced mono (x-height 6px) inside a bordered chip — the same rung as the 12px uppercase label column opposite them. All three are short categorical enums, so the split does not track data type and a reader cannot infer what the chip means. The chip is also the page's smallest type, applied to values, next to labels of the same size.

findings.location: Overview grid, AGE row value (690,1000)-(855,1018)
findings.finding: Carried and strengthened. `No timestamp published` — 22 characters of English, the grid's only honest-absence statement — is set at 12px letterspaced monospace inside the chip the page reserves for one-word machine tokens, making it the smallest type on a 2840px page and two rungs below the values it sits among. Letterspaced mono makes a sentence read as a value the chain emitted, which is the opposite of what the row exists to say. It should be set unchipped in the body face at the value rung.

findings.location: section rules: full-width hairlines at y=716, 1314, 1675 and 2290, above Overview (506,747), Decoded input (506,1345) and Raw (506,2321); no rule above Internal calls (506,1885) or State changes (506,2064)
findings.finding: Carried and re-verified. All six section headings are identical — 17px cap height, bold, same colour — so the hairline is the only heading-level signal on the page, and it falls above four of six peers. The resulting groups are {Overview}, {Decoded input}, {Events, Internal calls, State changes}, {Raw}: three sections read as one block whose members look exactly like the three that stand alone. The grouping also cuts against the page's own copy, which says Events comes from the receipt while the two beneath it come from the trace. With eight sections in one scroll the heading treatment has to be navigable without reading; here it groups without saying so.

findings.location: hero (506,200)-(1150,310) versus Overview grid FINALITY row (687,1084)
findings.finding: Carried. The expectation block places the finality badge in the hero; the hero carries only the `Succeeded` status badge, the truncated hash and the copy box. Finality appears nine rows down as `Pending`, at the 12px chip rung shared with CANONICAL, so a reader who takes the hero and the primary action — the top 440px — sees an unqualified success and no signal that the transaction is not yet final. Recorded P2 and not P1 because the badge is present, labelled and legible: its position in the hierarchy is wrong, not the information.

findings.location: hero H1 `0x27a6…9a6c` (506,236)-(712,259) against the section headings, e.g. Overview (506,747)-(600,763)
findings.finding: Downgraded from P2 after measurement. The H1's figure height is 24px against the headings' 17px cap height — a 1.41x step that does read as two levels, so last round's `effectively one level` no longer holds. What remains is a weight inversion: the H1's stems measure 3px on a 24px glyph (0.125) while the headings' measure 3-4px on a 17px cap (0.21), so the single level-one title is the lightest relative stroke on the page and the six repeated level-two headings are the heaviest. Size and weight still pull in opposite directions; the step now survives it.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · MANA row value (687,1185)-(960,1205)
findings.finding: Downgraded from P2. `42000  /  100000 mana (FeeJuice)` sets two quantities joined by a bare slash with no sub-label distinguishing usage from limit, and neither figure is grouped, so two five- and six-digit magnitudes must be compared digit by digit. The used/limit slash is a widely-read explorer idiom and the figures are correctly tabular mono with the unit dropped to the proportional muted face, so this is a refinement rather than a failure. Note also that the round's label humanisation is not visible here: the only cost label on this view is `COST · MANA` and the label column is uppercase, so a humanised source string would still render `COST · TRANSACTION FEE`.

findings.location: footer disclosure line (506,2740)-(1416,2780)
findings.finding: Carried. The disclosure sets roughly 130 characters on its first line across a 920px column, about double the ~70-character measure the provenance sentences (687,825), the trace note (528,465) and the three section notes hold to. Two lines, so it is readable; it is the one place on the page where prose is set to its container rather than to a measure.

findings.location: copy affordance, hero (506,276)-(925,308) and the `click to select` caption at (935,288)
findings.finding: Carried. The full hash sits at ~16px monospace, regular weight, on a white fill inside a hairline rounded border, with the gesture named by a 13px grey caption set outside the box. Nothing in the weight or the caption's prominence says the box is pressable; it reads as a read-only field displaying the value. A caption in the label register, or the value at control weight, would resolve it.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) code block, lines at y=2375, 2398, 2423, 2446, 2467, 2490
findings.finding: Carried and measured. Line pitch is 23px on ~14px monospace (~1.64), the body-prose line-height applied to code, while one indent level is two spaces — about 17px. The lines therefore sit further apart than the indentation is wide, so the nesting reads weaker than it is in the page's only preformatted region. A pitch near 20px would let the indent structure carry.

findings.location: page right edge — trace card (x504-1203, y359-610), decoded-input note (x504-1203, y1479-1572), Events note (y1756-1828), Internal calls note (y1935-2007), State changes note (y2114-2187), against the section rules at y716/1314/1675/2290, both facts grids (y779-1213, y1377-1451), the raw <pre> (y2357-2519), the nav resolver field and the footer content — all of which end at x=1415
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 and re-measured to the pixel: the column has two right edges 212px apart, alternating down the whole scroll. Every bordered panel carrying prose stops at x=1203; every rule, grid, the raw block and both pieces of site chrome run to x=1415. The left edges agree exactly at x=504, so the reader cannot read the 1203 edge as a narrower measure — it reads as a container that failed to fill. The four section rules make it worst: each is a 912px hairline drawn straight across a stack whose visible card edges stop 212px short of it.

findings.location: section headings — Overview (baseline y764, grid top y779), Decoded input (y1362 / y1377), Raw (chain-native) (y2337 / y2357) versus Events (y1723 / y1756), Internal calls (y1902 / y1935), State changes (y2081 / y2114)
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: one relationship is set at three values on one page. Heading baseline to the top of its first content is 15px where that content is a facts grid, 20px where it is the raw <pre>, and 33px where it is a notice card. The gap tracks the component that follows rather than the heading, so the same heading level binds tightly to a grid and loosely to a card, and the six sections do not read as peers. Pick one value — 24px would sit on the scale the rest of the page uses (30px rule-to-heading, 56px card-to-heading, ~102px section-to-section).

findings.location: hero — `Succeeded` badge at x724-833, y232-262 — versus the Overview grid's FINALITY row, `Pending` badge at x680-750, y1067-1100
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 and re-measured: 837px of vertical separation, with eight grid rows between them. Status and finality are one judgement about whether this transaction counts, and proximity here says they are unrelated. §7.2 places the finality badge in the hero beside the status; the hero has room — the h1 plus badge end at x=833 and the row is empty to x=1415. Moving `Pending` beside `Succeeded` also removes the page's only badge pair separated by more than the viewport height.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the provenance paragraph occupying y817-914, text ink x529-1121, against the label column fill x505-665 and the nine value cells whose text starts at x=690
findings.finding: New. The provenance sentences start at x=529 — the label column's own text edge — while every value in both grids starts at x=690, so the longest passage on the page is the one item in the grid that does not sit in the value column. Because the paragraph spans the full 912px, it also punches a 97px white gap (y817-914) through the label column's continuous grey band, which otherwise runs unbroken from y780 to y1213; a reader scanning the label column hits a hole four rows from the top. Either indent the paragraph to x=690 so it belongs to the DATA row's value cell, or drop the label-column fill for the whole DATA group so the break is deliberate rather than a leak.

findings.location: `Internal calls` heading (cap top y1885) between the Events card ending y1828 and its own card starting y1935; `State changes` heading (cap top y2063) between the Internal calls card ending y2007 and its own card starting y2114
findings.finding: New. Both headings are equidistant from the section above and the content below — 57px above / 50px below, and 56px / 51px — which is the failure §5 A2 names verbatim. Neither heading has a rule above it (Overview, Decoded input, Events and Raw all do), so spacing is the only grouping signal available and it is not being used: at a glance the heading reads as trailing the previous card as readily as introducing its own. Cutting the below-gap to the 24-33px band the other four sections use, or widening the above-gap toward the ~102px section rhythm, would settle it.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column — badge borders at x=680 (DATA y798, AGE y1007, CANONICAL y1045, FINALITY y1083) versus plain value text at x=690 (BLOCK, TYPE, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA)
findings.finding: Carried from vd9-r1 and worth accepting rather than fixing. The value column's visible left edge alternates between x=680 and x=690 over nine rows. It is defensible: each badge's own text begins at x=689-691, so the offset is a deliberate negative inset that makes the badge's letters align with the plain values, which is the more important edge. Recording it so the next reviewer does not re-derive it as a defect.

findings.location: trace card, the inner hairline at y548 (x529-1179) between the three-line explanation (ink ending y519) and the line `Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.` (ink starting y566)
findings.finding: New. The divider is not centred in the space it divides: roughly 26px of clearance above it and 13px below, once line boxes rather than ink are accounted for. It therefore reads as attached to the sentence beneath it rather than as a separator between two zones of one card, which is at odds with the card's otherwise symmetric 25/24px horizontal and 28px vertical padding.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block, x504-1415, y2357-2519 — text ink x531-1040, y2375-2503
findings.finding: New. The one preformatted region on the page uses 27px of horizontal padding against roughly 16-18px vertical, so its content sits noticeably closer to the top and bottom edges than to the left. Every other bordered surface on the page is padded evenly (notice cards 24/24 with 19px ink inset; facts-grid cells 25px). Equalising to 24px would bring the block onto the same inset as its neighbours.

findings.location: hero — h1 ink ends x711, `Succeeded` badge border starts x724; trace card — `Generate trace` button ends x679, `On demand` chip border starts x696
findings.finding: Carried from vd9-r1. The page's two control-plus-chip pairs use different gaps, 13px and 17px, 150px apart vertically. Both pairs are otherwise well set — the badge's bottom edge y262 lands on the h1 baseline, and the chip's vertical centre y410 matches the button's y411 — so a single 16px gap would finish them.

findings.location: Overview grid, value cells of the Age, Canonical and Finality rows
findings.finding: One chip token — fill #F3F3F3, border #C8C8C8, text #565656 — carries three unrelated meanings: an absent datum ("No timestamp published"), an affirmative fact ("Yes") and an in-progress state ("Pending"). The palette demonstrably has the tones to separate them: the hero's Succeeded chip is #DCFCE7 / #16A34A / #166534 and the Data badge is #DBEAFE / #2563EB / #1E40AF. Canonical: Yes is a confirmed positive rendered in the same grey as a missing value, so the grid's only three status cells are indistinguishable by colour and must all be read. Unchanged since round 1.

findings.location: Hero action card — Generate trace button (x 529-679) and the On demand chip (x 696-797)
findings.finding: Indigo #4F46E5 (hue 243, L 59%) and blue #2563EB (hue 221, L 53%) sit 16px edge to edge, 22 degrees and 6 lightness points apart. Last round measured 14px; the gap moved by 2px and the hue relationship did not change, so the finding stands. The chip compounds it: white fill, 1px saturated #2563EB border, #1E40AF label — the only outline pill on a page whose other three chips (Succeeded, Data, the grey trio) are all tinted-fill. Outline-pill-beside-filled-button is the standard secondary-button pattern, so a non-interactive state label reads as the second half of a button pair, and the indigo/blue distinction the design relies on is not perceivable at that separation.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block, y 2353-2524; also the hero hash chip and the Overview grid cell borders
findings.finding: The border token family sits below the 3:1 non-text floor on every surface it is used on, and worst where it carries the most load. The Raw block is the only container on the page with no fill — it is #ECECEB, identical to the canvas — so a 1px #A2A2A2 hairline at 2.16:1 is the sole thing containing the largest, densest region on the page. Unchanged since round 1, to the second decimal. The same #A2A2A2 reaches only 2.55:1 on the white note panels, the hero hash chip's #C8C8C8 boundary is 1.67:1 on white despite being the click-to-select affordance, and the grid's internal separators are the same 1.67:1. Three container treatments coexist: the hero card (white, shadow, no border), the notes and grid (white, hairline, no shadow) and Raw (no fill, hairline).

findings.location: Overview grid, Data row — the Synthetic demo data badge
findings.finding: The badge the spec calls for "in the neutral tone" renders in the accent-blue family: fill #DBEAFE, border #2563EB, text #1E40AF. That is not this page's neutral tone — grey #F3F3F3 / #565656 is, and finding 1 shows it being spent on three rows that do not need it. The consequence is that the one element graded as content rather than decoration wears the same #2563EB as the hero's trace-state chip and sits one hue step from the primary action's #4F46E5, so a caveat about data provenance is drawn with accent weight and reads as a highlight. Contrast is fine (7.15:1); the tone assignment is the problem.

findings.location: Decoded input grid, RAW row value cell
findings.finding: New this round as a consequence of change (a). The em dash is drawn in #242424, the same full-emphasis value colour as the real selector directly above it, so "no payload" and "0x1a2b3c4d" carry identical weight. The page already has a muted treatment for absence — the Age row's #565656 chip — so it now states absence two ways. Setting the dash to #565656 would align it.

findings.location: Site nav resolver field, and the Overview / Decoded input grids' label column
findings.finding: #DDDDDD is both the fill of the page's only text input and the fill of every static label cell, and both carry a grey hairline. The one editable surface on the page is therefore the same colour as a read-only column, distinguished only by the placeholder's wording.

findings.location: Footer, right column — the heart in "Built with ♥ by Metacraft Labs"
findings.finding: The heart is #4F46E5, the same token as the three real links beside it, while the sentence around it is #484848. A reader scanning that column for links sees four indigo marks, one of which is decorative and not interactive.

findings.location: hero status badge at (725-835, y 232-262); AGE row y 989-1027 and FINALITY row y 1064-1102 in the Overview grid
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 and re-measured: the hero carries status alone. `Succeeded` sits at y=247; the age statement is 761px below it and the `Pending` finality badge 836px below it, both as grid rows. New this round: at 1920x1080 the fold falls at y=1080, which cuts the FINALITY row (1064-1102) in half, so the one fact that qualifies a green `Succeeded` is clipped at exactly the fold rather than merely below it. The information is present, so this is placement, not breakage — but the hero has 480px of unused width at x>1203 to carry both.

findings.location: Overview grid, x 503-1416, y 780-1214; Decoded input grid y 1375-1450; Raw block y 2344-2549
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: one label/value pair per 913px row at a 1920px viewport. The longest value on the page, the FEE PAYER hash at y=1195, ends at x=1043, so 373px — 40.9% — is empty on all nine rows, and the grid still costs 434px of scroll. The Raw JSON block repeats the ratio exactly (longest line ends x=1044). The page is now 2840px, 2.63 viewport heights, to deliver nine grid rows, five sentences and six lines of JSON, and the whole column is 913px of a 1920px viewport. Two pairs per row, or a narrower column with the freed width used, would remove roughly 200px of scroll without dropping anything.

findings.location: Events heading y=1704 through the State changes card ending y=2187
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 (475px reported there; 483px now, the 8px being downstream drift from the longer ABI note). Three headings and three identically shaped 700px cards spend 483px — 45% of a 1080px viewport — on 53 words: 19 in Events, 17 in Internal calls, 17 in State changes. My r1 count of 46 was low; correcting it makes the ratio worse, not better. The trace card already prints `Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.` at y=571, and the two lower cards restate it split in two. The identical card shape also makes the run read as one block rather than three sections.

findings.location: right edges: Overview grid, Decoded input grid and Raw block end at x=1416; trace card, ABI note and the three statement cards end at x=1203
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the column has two right edges 213px apart, alternating down the page. The cost is not only alignment — the ABI note at y 1475-1573 wraps to three lines against a 700px measure while the grid 25px above it runs to x=1416, so the narrower cards wrap early against unused column width.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block, x 503-1416, y 2344-2549
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the one preformatted region holds six lines whose longest reaches x=1044, so 41% of the block is empty and it carries a four-key transaction object with no receipt object beside it, which the expectation asks for. There is still no visible max-height, scroll container or copy control, so at realistic volume — a real receipt is hundreds of lines — this block would run the page height past 2840px unbounded.

findings.location: Overview grid label column, x 517-664, e.g. `COST · MANA` at y=1195
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the labels are roughly 10px uppercase, letterspaced, in a mid grey — the smallest and lightest text on the page — and they are the only wayfinding into a nine-row grid whose rows are 38px tall. The size budget is inverted: there is generous row height to scan by and the thing being scanned is set at the floor.

findings.location: DATA row and provenance note at the head of the Overview grid, y 780-914
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the DATA row plus its note stand 134px tall against 38px rows, 31% of the grid's height, so every scannable fact begins 134px into a grid the reader entered under the heading `Overview`. The note's own measure also stops at x=1121, leaving 295px of the row empty. A secondary size under the badge would keep the claim and return the row rhythm at the grid's head.

findings.location: Decoded input grid, RAW row, value at x 688-698, y 1414-1450
findings.finding: New, and a consequence of change (a). Replacing `0x` with `—` is the honest call — `0x` asserted a zero-length payload the tree does not have — but it leaves a 10px glyph occupying a 913px x 36px row, 98.9% empty, and it is the third idiom this page uses for the same idea within 570px of scroll: the AGE row states absence as a bordered chip reading `No timestamp published` (y=1008), the RAW row as a bare em dash, and the Events/Internal calls/State changes sections as prose cards. The AGE chip is the strongest of the three and is the page's own pattern; the em dash carries none of its specificity and relies on the note 25px below to do the explaining.

findings.location: Decoded input section, heading y=1329 through the note card ending y=1573
findings.finding: New, and a consequence of change (c). The section now spends 244px of scroll to report an eight-character selector: a 46px heading, a two-row 75px grid holding `0x1a2b3c4d` and an em dash, and a 98px three-line note. The note itself grew to 38 words and accounts for the page going from 2818px to 2840px. Its last clause, `An ABI would not help, and BlockTracer cannot yet be given one in any case.`, states two overlapping facts where one would do; the honesty gain over the previous promise is real, but it was bought with a line of scroll rather than by rewriting the sentence.

findings.location: hero, beside the H1 hash `0x27a6…9a6c`
findings.finding: The expected element places the finality badge in the hero; only the green `Succeeded` status badge is there. Finality renders as `Pending` in row six of the Overview grid, roughly 800px further down. In the explorer register the hero is the at-a-glance answer, and an affirmative-toned badge standing alone there reads as settled. Move the `Pending` finality badge next to `Succeeded` so the two qualify each other.

findings.location: section headings across the page body
findings.finding: The full-measure hairline section rule is applied to four of six peer headings: it sits above `Overview`, `Decoded input`, `Events` and `Raw (chain-native)`, but not above `Internal calls` or `State changes`. All six headings are the same type level, so the rule marks groups that do not exist and the eight-sections-in-one-scroll navigation cue stops being trustworthy. Apply the divider to every peer heading or to none.

findings.location: Decoded input grid, RAW row versus Overview grid, AGE row
findings.finding: The same facts-grid primitive speaks two dialects for absent data. The AGE row carries a labelled chip, `No timestamp published`, which is the voice the brief asks for. The RAW row carries a bare em dash. Both mean 'the tree holds nothing here', and the em dash is the less informative of the two and the one that most resembles a rendering failure. Give RAW a `No call data` chip in the AGE row's treatment; the explanatory note below then reinforces rather than rescues it.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the `Synthetic demo data` provenance chip
findings.finding: The provenance chip is the only accent-hued chip on the page: it takes the indigo/blue hue family that the primary `Generate trace` button, the breadcrumb links and the `102:0` block link all use. Its three grid siblings (`No timestamp published`, `Yes`, `Pending`) are neutral grey and `Succeeded` is green. The label is not contradicted — blue reads informational, not affirmative — so this is not a tone failure, but the marker borrows the brand's action hue for a statement that is neither an action nor a link. A distinct neutral-informational tone outside the link hue would let it read as fact.

findings.location: Decoded input, explanatory note under the grid
findings.finding: Two copy defects in the new sentence. `This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds` garden-paths — with the relative pronoun elided, `ABI BlockTracer` parses as a compound noun on first read; insert `that`. And `An ABI would not help, and BlockTracer cannot yet be given one in any case` ends weakly: `in any case` is redundant after `and`, and `yet` smuggles a roadmap promise into a statement of present fact. Suggest: `…so there are no parameters to decode. An ABI would not help here, and BlockTracer cannot be given one.`

findings.location: Overview grid, `COST · MANA` row

findings.location: hero card note, Internal calls note, State changes note

findings.location: hero card note versus footer data disclosure
findings.finding: The hero note says generating a trace `needs an account`; the footer on the same page opens `No account, no tracking`. findings.location: Hero, the line directly beneath the H1 — the bordered full-hash box (approx. x 504-920, y 278-308 in the 1920x2840 image) and the grey `click to select` label immediately to its right at approx. x 932-1025
findings.finding: The copy affordance for the full transaction hash is rendered as prose, not as a control. In the resting state there is no icon, no button and no border, fill or weight change to mark the box as interactive — the sole cue is a ~13px low-contrast grey label set outside the element it governs, which a reader scanning the hero will take for a caption rather than an instruction. It also names a smaller action than the one a block-explorer reader arrives expecting: `select`, not `copy`, so even a reader who does read it is told the page will do less for them than every competitor's hash row does. Compounding both, the container is a rounded, thin-bordered white field built to the same pattern as the resolver input in the fixed nav, so the assembly parses as a read-only text field with helper text rather than as the page's most-used action. Copying the hash is the single most-performed interaction on a transaction page and this is the page a competitor comparison lands on; every other control on the screen — `Generate trace`, the `102:0` block link, the footer links — is drawn as unambiguously actionable, which makes this one the outlier rather than the house style. This is the only MUST SHOW item on the page where present-versus-absent was a judgement call, and that is what makes it the weakest element here.

findings.location: Code pane gutter: ⊘ at x75-82 y310-316 (line 29) and ⊙ at x76-81 y380-386 (line 32)

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) inset code block, y1048-1074
findings.finding: The mask is applied to the pane body, not to the ink, so it erases surface levels as well as text. The reversal is the damaging part: the page canvas immediately below the pane border is #ECECEB, darker than the faded block above it, so the surface gets lighter approaching the edge and then abruptly darker past it, which reads as the block ending rather than continuing — the opposite of what the fade was added to say. Fix: scope the mask to the scrolling content layer, or composite the gradient toward the block's own #ECECEB rather than toward transparent.

findings.location: Notice card, first sentence, against the reason directly beneath it; and the Internal calls / State changes empty-state notes

findings.location: Overview grid, CANONICAL row (`Yes`) and AGE row (`No timestamp published`) — adjacent rows, 30px apart

One states an affirmative fact about the transaction ('it is canonical'); the other states that a datum does not exist. Because FINALITY immediately below uses the green affirmative pill, the grid teaches the reader 'green = affirmative, grey = missing' across AGE and FINALITY, then contradicts it one row up at CANONICAL. `Yes` is also the only ordinary scalar value in the grid rendered as a chip at all — TYPE renders `public` as plain mono, COST renders plain text — so the neutral tone is spent here without encoding anything.

findings.location: `Succeeded` (page title row), `Finalized` (Overview FINALITY row), `Real Aztec mainnet data` (Overview DATA row)
findings.finding: One tone, three meanings on three different subject axes. Giving a content-grade provenance claim the same token as a routine status pill removes the one cue that would tell a reader it is a different kind of statement. findings.location: Notice card, the `Not observable` badge

resolutions.reason: P3. The two widths are a decision, not raggedness: data panels take the column (--bt-layout-container), prose panels take one shared prose width (--bt-layout-prose). This is a recorded TENSION rather than an agreement — L2 asked twice for the trace panel to be narrowed to its content (round 3) and then for one right edge (round 5), and those cannot both hold. The narrowing won because a 910px box around a 150px button and two sentences made the container outweigh the control it holds. What WAS fixed is the accidental part: the two prose panels previously sat at different widths because --bt-measure-prose is in `ch` and they were set at different font sizes; both now use one px token, so the page has two widths rather than three.

P3. The 92px vs 100px difference is margin collapsing between the trace card's box and the following section's margin-top, not a second spacing step: both are --bt-rhythm-section. Correcting it would mean giving one boundary a hand-written offset, which is the class of ad-hoc margin the rhythm roles exist to eliminate. Read and declined.

P3, and a genuine conflict between two readings from the same lens two rounds apart. Round 2's L2 reported that the badge's TEXT started 10px right of the other values and asked for text alignment; round 5's L2 reports that the badge's BOX starts 9px left of the other values and asks for box alignment. They are the same 9px and cannot both be satisfied while a badge has padding. Text alignment was kept, because the value column is read as a column of values and the badge's label is the value. Recorded rather than silently chosen.

P3. The full hash reads as an unlabelled value because it IS unlabelled — the hero's specified treatment (a copy affordance, an age, a finality badge beside it) is exactly the content VD.4 owns, and giving the line a foundations-level flourish now would decorate a hero that is about to be rebuilt around it. The typographic half is done: it sits at --bt-type-identifier-lead-size, one rung above the 14px data mono, in --bt-text-strong.

P3, and deliberate. The H1 is monospace because it IS an identifier — the change that made the page's largest type carry the page's actual subject, which three reviewers across two campaigns asked for.
